candidate.title: Transport behavior-conditioned residuals while preserving endpoint separation
candidate.equation: Let r_i=t_i-s_i and let p_s(c)=softmax_c(-||s_i-e_c||^2/tau), p_t(c)=softmax_c(-||t_i-e_c||^2/tau). Define v_s=sum_c p_s(c)e_c and v_t=sum_c p_t(c)e_c. Minimize L=w*mean_i[|| (v_t-v_s)-gamma*r_i ||^2 + lambda*max(0,m-||v_t-v_s||)^2 + eta*max(0,||v_t-v_s||-M)^2]. The first term transports the behavior-conditioned residual in codebook space; the lower and upper bounds prevent endpoint convergence and excessive transport.

symbols.p_s(c): Differentiable soft assignment of the source to code c.
symbols.p_t(c): Differentiable soft assignment of the target to code c.
symbols.gamma: Scale mapping the representation residual into codebook-space transport.
symbols.lambda: Weight on the minimum endpoint-separation constraint.
symbols.m: Minimum permitted distance between endpoint codebook representations.
symbols.eta: Weight on the maximum transport constraint.
symbols.M: Maximum permitted distance between endpoint codebook representations.
symbols.w: Weight composing this mechanism with the training objective.

candidate.behaviour_signal: The behavior-conditioned residual t_i-s_i, available from the source and target pair.
candidate.codebook_interaction: The transport term moves the two soft-assignment-weighted codebook representations so their displacement follows the representation residual. The minimum-distance hinge pushes them apart whenever their separation is too small; the maximum-distance hinge limits excessive displacement. Thus the transport target is a directed residual vector, not a shared code for both endpoints, and the lower bound explicitly prevents pair convergence.
candidate.encoder_interaction: The residual and soft assignments produce encoder gradients for both endpoints, but the host discards those gradients unless the mechanism reaches the codebook. This objective reaches the codebook through both endpoint soft assignments, so SID changes do not depend on retaining the encoder gradient.
candidate.risk: The representation residual may encode nuisance variation rather than recommendation-relevant behavior, and its direction or scale may not match useful codebook displacement. The bounds could preserve separation yet still yield an unhelpful hard partition, or the residual transport could increase train-to-test drift.
candidate.falsifier: The candidate is wrong if it fails to raise pair-level ER, if the median selected endpoint codeword separation decreases, or if the exported codes violate any control constraint: level-0 Gini, L1-to-L2 branches per code, train-to-test frequency drift, sequence information, or Stage-3 recall@10.
candidate.why_not_the_measured_failures: Unlike mechanisms whose only effective gradients were overwritten encoder gradients, this objective directly differentiates through codebook soft assignments. Unlike the collapsed arm, it transports a directed residual between endpoint representations rather than pulling both toward one code, and its explicit minimum-separation hinge opposes codeword convergence.
